scope: XMemVirtualAlloc write-watch profile 1, XMemGetWriteWatch ordinal 17, XMemResumeWriteWatch ordinal 24, and the supported write-watch suspension option (0x10000) in XMemSetOption ordinal 27. Other console options are not implemented.
native_method: Runs the hash-pinned console query, option and resume routines in a temporary mapped PE. Its imported GetWriteWatch is replaced with a native six-argument stub, and the harness checks the paused and resumed transitions.
native_result: xmem-native-watch PASS forwarded=6 paused=1003 output=untouched option=2 resume=3
guest_checks: Reserve and commit four Windows write-watch pages, write two and compare the XMem query against the host GetWriteWatch result and surrounding guards.
Reset through XMemGetWriteWatch, modify a different page, check the new result and compare invalid flag behavior with the host. Verify name and ordinal 17 identity.

Set suspension option 0x10000: paused queries return 1003 without writes, resume fails while suspension is requested, clearing the low 32-bit option value leaves queries paused until successful resume. Verify ordinals 24 and 27 and reject unsupported options.
Allocate write-watch regions via XMemVirtualAlloc in both reserve+commit and reserve-then-commit modes; modify pages and check the dirty-page result.
limits: Only option ID 0x10000 is supported. Other IDs return ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED and are not claimed as complete XMemSetOption behavior.
XMemVirtualAlloc supports only the two checked CPU write-watch profiles; other page-protection and Xbox-specific modes remain unsupported.
The native reference controls use stub GetWriteWatch and NtAllocateVirtualMemoryEx. Real console OS allocation and cross-thread behavior have not been measured.

native_allocation_method: Invokes the hash-pinned supplied allocator with standard NT mode and controlled NtAllocateVirtualMemoryEx and memset callbacks. For reserve plus commit with PAGE_READWRITE, and reserve only with PAGE_NOACCESS, MEM_WRITE_WATCH passes through unchanged both with and without MEM_TOP_DOWN. The NT callback is a stub; native success-path OS allocation was not executed.
